items.stem: Plan an extended response to the question: "Nationalism has done more harm than good." To what extent do you agree? Give a thesis, two arguments with specific evidence, a counter-argument and a conclusion.
items.answer: Thesis: Nationalism has caused great harm when exclusive and aggressive, but civic and anti-colonial nationalism have also achieved freedom and democracy; its effects depend on its form.
items.markingKey: Arguments for: it fuelled wars, including the First World War, and the persecution of minorities; ethnic nationalism has excluded and harmed people seen as outsiders. items.stem: Outline one way in which the Ems Telegram (1870) shows Realpolitik.
items.answer: Bismarck edited a report of a meeting between King Wilhelm and the French ambassador to make it seem insulting; France declared war. Manipulating news provoked a war that united the German states against France.
items.markingKey: Context (Bismarck edited a report of a meeting between King Wilhelm and the French ambassador to make it seem insulting; France declared war.) – 1 mark for accurate, specific detail. Link: manipulating news provoked a war that united the German states against France. – remaining marks for explicitly connecting the example to Realpolitik.

items.stem:
Source A – Historian's book (paraphrased): Paraphrase of Christopher Clark, "The Sleepwalkers: How Europe Went to War in 1914", 2012

The historian argued that the outbreak of war in 1914 was not the fault of one power. The leaders of every major state were like sleepwalkers – watchful but unseeing – moving step by step into a catastrophe that none of them fully intended.

Identify two points that Source A makes about nationalism as a cause of conflict and the road to 1914, using evidence from the source.
items.answer: All the great powers shared responsibility, stumbling into a war none fully wanted.
items.markingKey: All the great powers shared responsibility, stumbling into a war none fully wanted. Award 1 mark per relevant point drawn from the source, up to [3]; own knowledge is not credited here. Criterion D: interpreting a source.

items.stem: In which century did the founding of the Muslim League (1906 CE) take place?
items.answer: 20th century CE
items.markingKey: C. 1906 CE falls in the 20th century CE: e.g. the 15th century CE runs from 1401 to 1500.

items.stem:
Source A – Lecture (paraphrased): Paraphrase of Ernest Renan, lecture "What is a Nation?", Sorbonne, Paris, 1882

The speaker argued that a nation is not defined by race, language, religion or geography alone. It is a soul, a spiritual principle, made of a shared past of glory and sacrifice and a present desire to live together. A nation's existence is a daily plebiscite.

Outline the main argument or view that Source A presents, quoting or referring to the source.
items.answer: A nation rests on shared memories and the will to live together, not on race or language.
items.markingKey: A nation rests on shared memories and the will to live together, not on race or language. Award 1 mark per relevant point drawn from the source, up to [3]; own knowledge is not credited here. Criterion D: interpreting a source.

items.stem: On a timeline, the Frankfurt Parliament meets is marked at 1848 CE and the Austro-Prussian War at 1866 CE. Calculate the number of years between the two events.
items.answer: 18 years
items.markingKey: 18 by subtraction (M1 A1). BCE years count down towards 1 BCE; the year after 1 BCE is 1 CE.

items.stem: Hana argues that "Nationalism was the most important long-term cause of the First World War." Omar disagrees. Explain one piece of evidence each student could use, and state which view you find more convincing and why.
items.answer: Nationalism was a key underlying cause and created the spark, but alliances and militarism explain why a Balkan crisis became a world war.
items.markingKey: Hana: Balkan nationalism created the crisis that started the war. Omar: the alliance system turned a local war into a European war. Judgement (1-2 marks): Nationalism was a key underlying cause and created the spark, but alliances and militarism explain why a Balkan crisis became a world war.

items.stem: Analyse one strength and one limitation of this view: "Non-violent protest was the most important reason why India gained independence in 1947."
items.answer: Non-violent mass protest was central in creating a nationwide demand, but independence in 1947 also depended on Britain's post-war weakness and other forms of pressure.
items.markingKey: Arguments for: satyagraha built a mass movement and won international sympathy; it made British rule morally and practically harder to sustain. Arguments against: the Second World War weakened Britain economically and militarily; the 1946 naval mutiny, revolutionary movements and Bose's INA showed British control of the army was weakening. Supported judgement: Non-violent mass protest was central in creating a nationwide demand, but independence in 1947 also depended on Britain's post-war weakness and other forms of pressure.

items.stem:

The speaker argued that a nation is not defined by race, language, religion or geography alone. It is a soul, a spiritual principle, made of a shared past of glory and sacrifice and a present desire to live together. A nation's existence is a daily plebiscite.

Explain one value and one limitation of Source A for an investigation into nationalism: nation, state, identity and national symbols, referring to its origin and purpose.
items.answer: Origin: Paraphrase of Ernest Renan, lecture "What is a Nation?", Sorbonne, Paris, 1882. Purpose: to argue that nations are based on shared will, partly in response to Germany's annexation of Alsace-Lorraine. Value: It is a classic statement of civic nationalism by an influential thinker. Limitation: It was shaped by French interests: Renan wanted to argue that Alsace was French despite its German dialect.

items.stem: A class brainstorm on nationalism as a cause of conflict and the road to 1914 produced the question "Why do wars happen?" Explain why it needs refining, then suggest an improved research question and justify your change.

items.stem: Which movement did Gandhi launch on 8 August 1942?
items.answer: Quit India
items.markingKey: C. Its slogan was "Do or die".

items.stem: Which of the following best describes "nation"?
options: Two wars in 1912–13 in which Balkan states fought the Ottoman Empire and then each other
The 1920–22 campaign of boycotting British institutions, goods and honours, called off after violence at Chauri Chaura
"little Germany": a united Germany without Austria, led by Prussia
A large group of people who share a sense of common identity, often based on language, culture, history or territory
items.answer: A large group of people who share a sense of common identity, often based on language, culture, history or territory
items.markingKey: D. "nation" is a large group of people who share a sense of common identity, often based on language, culture, history or territory.

items.stem: Where was the German Empire proclaimed on 18 January 1871?
options: The Hall of Mirrors at Versailles
items.answer: The Hall of Mirrors at Versailles
items.markingKey: A. It was a humiliation for defeated France.

items.stem: Explain the difference between a long-term cause and the immediate cause of the First World War.
items.answer: Long-term causes include nationalism, alliances, militarism and imperial rivalry; the immediate cause was the assassination of Franz Ferdinand on 28 June 1914 and the July Crisis that followed.
items.markingKey: Long-term causes include nationalism, alliances, militarism and imperial rivalry; the immediate cause was the assassination of Franz Ferdinand on 28 June 1914 and the July Crisis that followed. One mark for a correct account of each side; further marks for making the difference explicit (not two separate definitions).

items.stem: Diego writes: "All Indians supported Congress." Explain why this is inaccurate.
items.answer: The Muslim League, many princely rulers and some Dalit leaders had different aims and concerns.
items.markingKey: The Muslim League, many princely rulers and some Dalit leaders had different aims and concerns. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: Explain why the boundaries of nations and states often do not match.
items.answer: Borders were drawn by wars, empires and treaties that ignored where peoples lived, so some nations are split across states and some states contain many nations.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: Borders were drawn by wars, empires and treaties that ignored where peoples lived, so some nations are split across states and some states contain many nations. (2 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

items.stem: "Italy and Germany were unified mainly by popular revolutions." Explain the flaw in this statement.
items.answer: The 1848 revolutions failed; unification came mainly through the diplomacy and wars of Piedmont and Prussia, though popular nationalism helped.
items.markingKey: The 1848 revolutions failed; unification came mainly through the diplomacy and wars of Piedmont and Prussia, though popular nationalism helped. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: Briefly explain why Russia supported Serbia.
items.answer: As the leading Slavic and Orthodox power, Russia claimed to protect Slavs (Pan-Slavism) and wanted influence in the Balkans and access to the Straits; after backing down in 1908 it was unwilling to do so again.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: As the leading Slavic and Orthodox power, Russia claimed to protect Slavs (Pan-Slavism) and wanted influence in the Balkans and access to the Straits; after backing down in 1908 it was unwilling to do so again. (2 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

items.stem: Explain why the Jallianwala Bagh massacre strengthened the national movement.
items.answer: The shooting of hundreds of unarmed people, and the support Dyer received in Britain, convinced many moderate Indians that British rule could not be reformed; Rabindranath Tagore returned his knighthood.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: The shooting of hundreds of unarmed people, and the support Dyer received in Britain, convinced many moderate Indians that British rule could not be reformed; Rabindranath Tagore returned his knighthood. items.stem: Write one well-structured paragraph (Point, Evidence, Explanation, Link) in answer to this question: Explain why language has often been central to nationalism.
items.answer: A shared language allows communication, literature and newspapers that build common identity; nationalists such as the Grimm brothers collected folk tales to show a shared culture.

items.stem: Explain why "How important was Prussia's economic strength in the unification of Germany between 1834 and 1871?" is a suitable research question for an MYP investigation into the unification of Italy and Germany.

items.stem: Rafael argues that "Nationalism has done more harm than good." Elena disagrees. Explain one piece of evidence each student could use, and state which view you find more convincing and why.
items.answer: Nationalism has caused great harm when exclusive and aggressive, but civic and anti-colonial nationalism have also achieved freedom and democracy; its effects depend on its form.
items.markingKey: Rafael: it fuelled wars, including the First World War, and the persecution of minorities. Elena: it inspired movements for self-determination and freedom from empire. Judgement (1-2 marks): Nationalism has caused great harm when exclusive and aggressive, but civic and anti-colonial nationalism have also achieved freedom and democracy; its effects depend on its form.

items.stem:
Source A – Speech to a parliamentary committee (paraphrased): Paraphrase of Otto von Bismarck, speech to the Budget Committee of the Prussian Landtag, 30 September 1862

The minister-president told the Prussian budget committee that Germany did not look to Prussia's liberalism but to its power. The great questions of the day would not be decided by speeches and majority votes – that had been the mistake of 1848 and 1849 – but by iron and blood.

How reliable is Source A for someone researching the unification of Italy and Germany? Justify your answer using its origin and purpose.
items.answer: Origin: Paraphrase of Otto von Bismarck, speech to the Budget Committee of the Prussian Landtag, 30 September 1862. Purpose: to persuade liberal deputies to approve army spending. Value: It shows Bismarck's own view of how unification would be achieved, early in his career. Limitation: It was a speech meant to win a budget argument and caused outrage at the time; it should not be read as a full plan.

items.stem:
Source A – Book (paraphrased): Paraphrase of M. K. Gandhi, "Hind Swaraj" (Indian Home Rule), written in 1909 as a dialogue

The author argued that India had not been taken by the English; Indians had given it to them by cooperating with British rule. If Indians stopped cooperating – in trade, courts, schools and government – British power would end. True swaraj meant ruling ourselves, not simply replacing English rulers with Indian ones.

"Non-violent protest was the most important reason why India gained independence in 1947." Using Source A and your own knowledge, to what extent do you agree?
items.answer: Non-violent mass protest was central in creating a nationwide demand, but independence in 1947 also depended on Britain's post-war weakness and other forms of pressure.
items.markingKey: From the source: British rule depends on Indian cooperation; withdrawing it would bring real self-rule. Own knowledge for: satyagraha built a mass movement and won international sympathy; it made British rule morally and practically harder to sustain. Own knowledge against: the Second World War weakened Britain economically and militarily; the 1946 naval mutiny, revolutionary movements and Bose's INA showed British control of the army was weakening. Judgement: Non-violent mass protest was central in creating a nationwide demand, but independence in 1947 also depended on Britain's post-war weakness and other forms of pressure. items.stem: Write the introduction and an outline of the body paragraphs for an essay that evaluates the view that "Bismarck was the main reason for the unification of Germany."
items.answer: Thesis: Bismarck was the decisive individual, but he succeeded because of Prussian economic and military power and favourable international circumstances.
items.markingKey: Arguments for: his diplomacy isolated each enemy and his wars removed the obstacles; he manipulated events such as the Ems Telegram. Counter-arguments: Prussia's economic strength (Zollverein, coal, railways) and army reforms made victory possible; nationalist feeling and the mistakes of Austria and France also mattered. Thesis/conclusion: Bismarck was the decisive individual, but he succeeded because of Prussian economic and military power and favourable international circumstances. Credit a thesis that answers the question, logically ordered paragraphs each with specific evidence, a counter-argument that is weighed, and a conclusion that follows. Criterion C (communicating): appropriate style and register for the purpose, a clear structure suited to the format (topic sentence, developed evidence, explanation, link back to the question), accurate subject terminology, and sources documented with a recognised convention (MLA or APA).

items.stem: Write the introduction and an outline of the body paragraphs for an essay that evaluates the view that "Nationalism was the most important long-term cause of the First World War."
items.answer: Thesis: Nationalism was a key underlying cause and created the spark, but alliances and militarism explain why a Balkan crisis became a world war.
items.markingKey: Arguments for: Balkan nationalism created the crisis that started the war; nationalist public opinion pushed governments towards confrontation. Counter-arguments: the alliance system turned a local war into a European war; militarism and war plans such as the Schlieffen Plan made escalation rapid. Thesis/conclusion: Nationalism was a key underlying cause and created the spark, but alliances and militarism explain why a Balkan crisis became a world war. Credit a thesis that answers the question, logically ordered paragraphs each with specific evidence, a counter-argument that is weighed, and a conclusion that follows.
